92ebd45f54333fc6f331fa28.excerpt: 인공지능(AI) 기술의 확산에 따라 AI를 단순히 도입하고 활용하는 단계를 넘어, 보안성과 안전성, 신뢰성, 사이버 복원력을 지속적으로 검증하는 ‘AI 보증(AI Assurance)’ 체계로 전환해야 한다는 필요성이 강조됐다.한국정보보호학회(KIISC)는 지난 10월 22일 서울 송파구 삼성SDS 웨스트캠퍼스 마젤란홀에서 ‘2026 KIISC 제6회 AI x RMF 워크숍’을 개최했다.이번 워크숍은 ‘Assuring AI: Security, Safety, Trustworthiness and Resilience in RMF’를 주제로
92ebd45f54333fc6f331fa28.title_ko: 한국정보보호학회, '2026 AI x RMF 워크숍' 개최
92ebd45f54333fc6f331fa28.summary_ko: 한국정보보호학회가 AI 시스템의 보안성과 신뢰성을 전 주기적으로 검증하는 'AI 보증' 체계 전환을 논의하는 워크숍을 개최했다. 행사에서는 위험관리 프레임워크(RMF) 기반의 AI 보안 대응 전략과 소버린 보안 생태계 구축 방안이 심도 있게 다뤄졌다.

curation.reason_ko: 한국정보보호학회가 AI 시스템의 보안성과 신뢰성을 전 주기적으로 검증하는 'AI 보증' 체계 전환을 논의했습니다.

590c21466ca59f5bf86cf242.excerpt: 삼성SDI가 26일 미주법인 '삼성SDI 아메리카(SDIA)가 미국의 에너지 전문기업인 알파오메가파워(AOP)와 1GWh 규모의 에너지저장장치(ESS) 솔루션 공급 계약을 체결했다고 26일 밝혔다. 앞서 지난해말 계약한 1차 물량까지 포함하면 총 1.5GWh 규모로, AOP는 삼성SDI로부터 공급받은 ESS 솔루션을 내년 텍사스주에서 착공하는 대규모 전력 프로젝트에 투입할 예정이다. 이번 계약에 따라 공급하게 될 제품은 삼원계(NCA) 배터리가
590c21466ca59f5bf86cf242.title_ko: 삼성SDI, 미국 에너지 기업에 AI 기반 ESS 솔루션 공급
590c21466ca59f5bf86cf242.summary_ko: 삼성SDI가 미국 알파오메가파워에 1.5GWh 규모의 에너지저장장치(ESS) 솔루션을 공급합니다. 공급되는 'SBB 1.7'은 AI 알고리즘을 활용한 이상 진단 및 수명 예측 기능을 갖추었으며, 강화된 화재 안전 표준을 충족했습니다.

curation.reason_ko: 삼성SDI가 AI 기반 이상 진단 및 수명 예측 기능을 갖춘 ESS 솔루션을 미국 에너지 기업에 공급합니다.

62561dd2d7a24646d2c4fd92.excerpt: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
62561dd2d7a24646d2c4fd92.title_ko: 클라우드플레어, 다단계 보안 감사를 위한 'security-audit-skill' 공개
62561dd2d7a24646d2c4fd92.summary_ko: 클라우드플레어(Cloudflare)가 공개한 'security-audit-skill'은 다단계 보안 감사를 수행하도록 설계된 코딩 에이전트용 기술입니다. 이 도구는 기계 판독이 가능한 감사 결과를 생성하고 이를 독립적으로 검증할 수 있도록 지원합니다.

curation.reason_ko: 클라우드플레어가 다단계 보안 감사를 수행하고 기계 판독 가능한 결과를 생성하는 AI 코딩 에이전트용 기술을 공개했습니다.

1b748d85801878668a0cc2e4.title_ko: 경찰청-씽크포비엘, AI 영향 평가 및 위험 관리 체계 구축
1b748d85801878668a0cc2e4.summary_ko: 경찰청이 씽크포비엘과 협력해 AI 기획부터 운영까지 전 과정을 관리할 수 있는 글로벌 수준의 위험 관리 체계를 마련했습니다. EU AI 법 및 국제 표준을 반영한 이 체계는 도입 적합성 판별, 신뢰성 검증, 운영 중단 조치 권한 등을 포함하며, 내년 법령 시행에 따른 공공기관의 AI 관리 의무에 대응할 계획입니다.

curation.reason_ko: 경찰청이 AI 도입 및 운영 전 과정의 위험을 관리하기 위해 씽크포비엘과 협력하여 체계를 마련했습니다.

089ec78a63d18db0e4f005a2.title_ko: 미래에셋생명, 시스템 침해로 인한 고객 개인정보 유출 확인
089ec78a63d18db0e4f005a2.summary_ko: 미래에셋생명은 외부 침입으로 인해 일부 고객의 신용정보가 유출된 사실을 확인했다고 밝혔다. 보험업권에서 발생한 첫 해킹 사례로, 현재 회사는 외부 전문기관과 협력하여 정확한 유출 항목과 대상을 분석 중이다.

curation.reason_ko: 미래에셋생명에서 시스템 침해 사고가 발생하여 고객 신용정보가 유출되었습니다.

8aab354ef49f774c988e303f.title_ko: 앤트로픽, 엘비스 프레슬리 노래 무단 학습 관련 저작권 소송 피소
8aab354ef49f774c988e303f.summary_ko: 엘비스 프레슬리 음악 권리자들이 앤트로픽을 상대로 약 540억 원 규모의 저작권 침해 소송을 제기했다. 원고 측은 앤트로픽이 허가 없이 노래 274곡을 학습 데이터로 사용하고, 저작권을 침해하는 결과물을 생성하도록 모델을 구축했다고 주장한다.

curation.reason_ko: 앤트로픽이 엘비스 프레슬리의 저작권을 침해했다는 이유로 거액의 손해배상 소송에 휘말렸습니다.

55ff863326643338a01bc5a1.title_ko: AI 코딩 에이전트 악용하는 악성 설정 파일 배포 주의
55ff863326643338a01bc5a1.summary_ko: 다운로드 폴더에 생성된 악성 지시 파일(AGENTS.md 등)을 AI 코딩 에이전트가 정상적인 설정으로 인식하여 악성 패키지를 설치하게 만드는 공격 방식이 발견되었다. 개발자가 에이전트를 다운로드 폴더에서 실행할 경우 웹을 통해 자동으로 생성된 파일이 에이전트의 제어권을 탈취할 위험이 있으므로 주의가 필요하다.

curation.reason_ko: 다운로드 폴더 내 악성 파일을 배치하여 AI 코딩 에이전트가 이를 설치하도록 유도하는 새로운 공격 기법이 보고되었습니다.

659a5a8584d66906bc37a48a.title_ko: AI 모델 백도어 탐지 및 제거를 위한 TopKLoRA 연구
659a5a8584d66906bc37a48a.summary_ko: AI 모델의 백도어를 해석하고 효율적으로 제거할 수 있는 'TopKLoRA' 미세조정 기법이 제안되었다. 이 방법은 희소(sparse) 어댑터를 사용하여 백도어 회로를 식별하고, 모델 성능 저하 없이 악성 기능을 외과적으로 ablation(절제)할 수 있도록 돕는다.

curation.reason_ko: TopKLoRA라는 기법을 통해 AI 모델 내 악성 백도어 회로를 식별하고 제거할 수 있는 해석 가능한 학습 방식을 제안했습니다.

1c141ca40a1b594e029298eb.title_ko: 웹 애플리케이션 취약점 검증을 위한 다중 에이전트 프레임워크 'Ulysses'
1c141ca40a1b594e029298eb.summary_ko: LLM이 생성한 웹 취약점의 진위를 스스로 검증하는 다중 에이전트 보안 프레임워크 'Ulysses'가 소개되었다. 이 프레임워크는 취약점 가설을 검증 가능한 증명(Proof of Exploitability)으로 변환하며, 실제 웹 환경에서 4개의 신규 취약점을 발견하는 성과를 거뒀다.

curation.reason_ko: 연구 논문에서 AI 에이전트를 활용해 웹 애플리케이션의 보안 취약점을 자동으로 탐지하고 검증하는 방안을 제시했습니다.

d2d038d4fa5a7996b761ea23.title_ko: 제논, 생성 AI 보안 위협 대응 위한 AI 가드레일 솔루션 '젠가드' 출시
d2d038d4fa5a7996b761ea23.summary_ko: 제논이 생성 AI 서비스의 보안 정책을 관리하고 탈옥 및 프롬프트 공격을 방어하는 '젠가드'를 출시했다. 이 솔루션은 모델 재학습 없이 자연어로 서비스별 맞춤 보안 정책 설정이 가능하며, 개인정보 마스킹 및 온프레미스 환경을 지원한다. 함께 공개된 자체 경량 모델 '젠가드 1.0 라이트'는 한국어 안전성 평가 데이터셋인 KSPG-Bench에서 우수한 성능과 처리 속도를 기록했다.

5fbde27308b7cc606fcedcb8.title_ko: 영국, AI 활용 생물보안 연구소 설립 및 사이버 방어 체계 구축에 대규모 투자

CVE-2026-96581.description: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key vulnerability in ash-project ash allows a user of one tenant to read, overwrite and take over another tenant's records via an upserting create action. Under attribute multitenancy, Ash.Actions.Create (lib/ash/actions/create/create.ex) and Ash.Actions.Create.Bulk (lib/ash/actions/create/bulk.ex) upserted on the primary key, or on an all_tenants? identity, without scoping the conflicting record to the request's tenant. A caller of a create action with upsert? true that accepts the primary key, supplying a record id from another tenant, updated that record's upsert fields and received all of its attributes in the result. With the default upsert fields the tenant attribute was written too, moving the record into the caller's tenant. Read and update policies do not run for upserts, and tenant-scoped create policies pass because the tenant is the caller's own. This issue affects ash: from 1.22.0 before 3.37.2.
CVE-2026-96581.summary_ko: ash-project ash 프레임워크의 upsert 작업에서 테넌트 간 권한 우회 취약점이 발견되었습니다. 공격자가 타 테넌트의 레코드를 읽거나 덮어쓰고, 자신의 테넌트로 가져올 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: ash-project의 다중 테넌트 환경에서 테넌트 격리 우회 및 레코드 탈취가 가능한 심각한 권한 부여 취약점입니다.

CVE-2026-116231.description: A security flaw has been discovered in Oray Pugongying X5 Pro 7.6.1. The impacted element is an unknown function of the component Ser2net. Performing a manipulation of the argument regmsg results in crlf injection. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
CVE-2026-116231.summary_ko: Oray Pugongying X5 Pro의 Ser2net 구성 요소에서 CRLF 주입 취약점이 발견되었습니다. 원격에서 인자 값을 조작하여 공격이 수행될 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Oray Pugongying 라우터에서 CRLF 주입을 통해 원격으로 시스템 명령 실행이 가능한 고위험 취약점입니다.

CVE-2026-115817.description: Starman versions before 0.4019 for Perl allow a stalled request body to hold a worker indefinitely, as read_timeout covers only the headers. Content-Length and chunked request bodies are read with blocking reads and no deadline. A client that sends complete headers and then stalls or trickles the body keeps the worker waiting until it disconnects. A remote attacker can take every worker with a few such connections, five with the default worker count, so the server stops answering requests. Version 0.4019 applies read_timeout to each wait for body data and adds a body_timeout limit, 300 seconds by default, on the total time to read a body.
CVE-2026-115817.summary_ko: Starman의 요청 본문 처리 과정에서 read_timeout 미비로 인해 워커가 무한 대기 상태에 빠질 수 있습니다. 원격 공격자가 이를 악용해 서버의 모든 워커를 점유하여 서비스 거부 상태를 유발할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Starman Perl 웹 서버에서 요청 처리 미비로 인해 서비스 거부 및 CPU/메모리 고갈을 유발할 수 있는 취약점들입니다.

CVE-2026-107894.description: V-SFT provided by FUJI ELECTRIC CO., LTD. contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability. Opening a crafted V7 file may lead to information exposure or arbitrary code execution on the affected product.

CVE-2026-116103.description: A vulnerability was identified in Sony Neural Network Libraries up to 1.39.0. This affects the function load_param_in_txt of the file python/src/nnabla/utils/cli/encode_decode_param.py of the component Encode Param Command Handler. Such manipulation leads to code injection. CVE-2026-116103.summary_ko: Sony Neural Network Libraries의 Encode Param Command Handler 내 load_param_in_txt 함수에서 코드 주입 취약점이 확인되었습니다. 원격 공격자가 이를 이용할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Sony Neural Network Libraries의 CLI 및 변환 도구에서 코드 주입 및 명령 실행 가능 취약점이 확인되었습니다.

CVE-2026-116106.description: A security vulnerability has been detected in HeyCyan App 1.0.103 on Android. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the component FileProvider. The manipulation leads to improper access controls. The attack may be initiated remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
CVE-2026-116106.summary_ko: Android용 HeyCyan App의 FileProvider 구성 요소에 부적절한 접근 제어 취약점이 있습니다. 원격에서 이를 조작하여 권한 범위를 벗어난 접근이 가능할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Android용 HeyCyan App에서 부적절한 파일 권한 관리 및 통신 보안 미비로 인한 정보 노출 취약점입니다.

CVE-2026-116114.description: A weakness has been identified in Yoosee GM8135S Camera 21.00.01.36. This affects an unknown function of the file /npc/npc of the component Live UDP H.264 Video Stream Handler. This manipulation causes cleartext transmission of sensitive information. The attack can be initiated remotely. The attack's complexity is rated as high. The exploitability is reported as difficult. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
CVE-2026-116114.summary_ko: Yoosee GM8135S 카메라의 라이브 UDP 영상 스트림 처리 기능에서 민감 정보가 평문으로 전송되는 취약점이 확인되었습니다. 원격에서 정보 탈취가 시도될 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Yoosee 카메라 소프트웨어에서 평문 전송, 부적절한 초기화, 보안 부팅 인증 우회 등 심각한 보안 결함이 발견되었습니다.

CVE-2026-116119.description: A vulnerability was found in NocoDB up to 2026.08.0. This affects an unknown part of the file packages/nocodb/src/services/users/users.service.ts of the component Password-Reset Flow. The manipulation results in race condition. The attack can be executed remotely. The vendor deleted the GitHub issue for this vulnerability without any explanation. Afterwards the vendor was contacted early about this disclosure via email but did not respond in any way.
CVE-2026-116119.summary_ko: NocoDB의 비밀번호 재설정 흐름에서 경쟁 상태(Race Condition) 취약점이 발견되었습니다. 원격에서 조작이 가능하며 잠재적인 보안 위험을 초래합니다.

curation.reason_ko: NocoDB의 인증 및 등록 흐름에서 레이스 컨디션 및 자원 관리 미흡으로 인한 취약점들이 발견되었습니다.

CVE-2026-116056.description: A flaw has been found in KodCloud KodExplorer up to 4.56. Affected is the function request_url_safe of the file app/function/web.function.php of the component Remote Download. This manipulation causes server-side request forgery. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
CVE-2026-116056.summary_ko: KodCloud KodExplorer의 원격 다운로드 컴포넌트 내 request_url_safe 함수에서 서버 측 요청 위조(SSRF) 취약점이 발견되었습니다. 원격에서 공격이 가능합니다.

curation.reason_ko: KodCloud KodExplorer의 파일 업로드 및 SSRF 취약점으로 원격 공격 가능성이 확인되었습니다.

CVE-2026-116096.description: A weakness has been identified in ggml-org llama.cpp. Affected by this issue is the function list_pockettts_state_slots of the file tools/mtmd/models/pockettts-gen.cpp of the component Pocket-TTS. This manipulation of the argument mmproj causes out-of-bounds write. The attack requires local access. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. Upgrading to version b11796 can resolve this issue. Patch name: 0a1ef309cdbb9f2024f58a38fb4c42352c5db569. The affected component should be upgraded. The reported heap out‑of‑bounds write (gen‑audio / pocket‑tts state_out path) is no longer a silent exploitable heap write on current master and the latest release b11871 - a malicious mmproj that previously triggered it now trips a release‑active GGML_ASSERT and aborts. But the submitter's recommended by‑construction fix (PR #29360 "prevent OOB accesses from malformed mmproj files") is still open. So the root cause is detected‑and‑aborted, not prevented‑by‑design.
CVE-2026-116096.summary_ko: llama.cpp의 Pocket-TTS 구성요소 내 list_pockettts_state_slots 함수에서 경계 외부 쓰기 취약점이 발견되었습니다. mmproj 파일 조작을 통해 발생하며 로컬 접근이 필요합니다.

curation.reason_ko: llama.cpp의 Pocket-TTS 컴포넌트 내에서 OOB 쓰기 및 메모리 조작이 가능한 취약점이 발견되었습니다.

CVE-2026-116095.description: A vulnerability was identified in smg-project smg 1.7.0/1.8.0/1.9.0/1.10.0/1.10.1. Affected is the function jpeg_turbo::decode_jpeg_rgb of the file crates/multimodal/src/jpeg_turbo.rs of the component llm-multimodal. The manipulation leads to uncontrolled memory allocation. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. Upgrading to version 1.11.0 is able to address this issue. The identifier of the patch is 8f51b57e219a914089e345b704c3c8de37a3bb8e. It is advisable to upgrade the affected component.
CVE-2026-116095.summary_ko: smg 프로젝트의 llm-multimodal 구성요소 내 jpeg_turbo::decode_jpeg_rgb 함수에서 비제어 메모리 할당 취약점이 확인되었습니다. 원격 공격이 가능하며 메모리 자원 고갈을 유발할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: smg 프로젝트의 llm-multimodal 라이브러리에서 비제어 메모리 할당으로 인한 DoS 취약점이 확인되었습니다.

CVE-2026-113345.description: Electronic delivery item Inspection Support System provided by Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism contains an improper file access permission vulnerability. CVE-2026-113345.summary_ko: 일본 국토교통성의 전자납품 검사지원시스템에 파일 접근 권한 설정 오류가 존재합니다. 설치 폴더 내 파일이 변조될 경우 임의 코드 실행으로 이어질 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: 일본 국토교통성 제공 시스템의 설치 폴더 내 파일 접근 권한 관리 미흡으로 인한 코드 실행 취약점입니다.

CVE-2026-116058.description: A vulnerability was found in Alfresco Activiti up to 7.21.0-rc.692. Affected by this issue is the function JuelScriptEngine.eval of the file JuelScriptEngine.java. Performing a manipulation results in code injection. The attack can be initiated remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
CVE-2026-116058.summary_ko: Alfresco Activiti의 JuelScriptEngine.java 파일 내 함수 조작으로 인해 원격 코드 인젝션이 발생할 수 있습니다. 원격에서 공격을 시작할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Alfresco Activiti의 엔진 구성 요소에서 원격 코드 인젝션이 가능한 취약점이 발견되었습니다.

CVE-2026-116094.description: A vulnerability was determined in EyouCMS up to 1.8.3. This impacts the function remote_file_to_local of the file application/function.php. Executing a manipulation can lead to server-side request forgery. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. CVE-2026-116094.summary_ko: EyouCMS의 application/function.php 내 remote_file_to_local 함수에서 서버 측 요청 위조(SSRF) 취약점이 발견되었습니다. 원격 공격자가 이를 악용할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: EyouCMS의 원격 파일 처리 함수에서 SSRF 공격이 가능한 취약점이 확인되었습니다.

CVE-2026-116063.description: A weakness has been identified in DedeCMS up to 5.7.118. Impacted is the function require_once of the file dede/update_guide.php. curation.reason_ko: DedeCMS의 업데이트 가이드 파일에서 코드 인젝션이 가능한 취약점이 확인되었습니다.

CVE-2026-116109.description: A vulnerability has been found in continuedev Continue 2.0.0. This vulnerability affects the function MCPManagerSingleton.setConnections of the file core/config/ConfigHandler.ts of the component MCP Server Transport. curation.reason_ko: Continue의 MCP 서버 구성 요소에서 운영체제 명령 주입 취약점이 발견되었습니다.

CVE-2026-103298.description: The CCAvenue Payment Gateway for WooCommerce WordPress plugin through 3.1 does not verify that a payment-confirmation request genuinely originates from the payment provider, and derives its verification key from a value that is empty on a default install, allowing unauthenticated attackers to forge a confirmation and mark any WooCommerce order as paid without payment.

curation.reason_ko: 다수의 워드프레스 결제 플러그인에서 결제 콜백 인증 미비로 인한 결제 위조 취약점이 발견되었습니다.

CVE-2026-116124.description: A security vulnerability has been detected in GNOME libgsf up to 1.14.60. curation.reason_ko: GNOME libgsf의 OLE2 파서에서 힙 버퍼 오버플로우가 가능한 취약점이 확인되었습니다.

92ebd45f54333fc6f331fa28.excerpt: 인공지능(AI) 기술의 확산에 따라 AI를 단순히 도입하고 활용하는 단계를 넘어, 보안성과 안전성, 신뢰성, 사이버 복원력을 지속적으로 검증하는 ‘AI 보증(AI Assurance)’ 체계로 전환해야 한다는 필요성이 강조됐다.한국정보보호학회(KIISC)는 지난 10월 22일 서울 송파구 삼성SDS 웨스트캠퍼스 마젤란홀에서 ‘2026 KIISC 제6회 AI x RMF 워크숍’을 개최했다.이번 워크숍은 ‘Assuring AI: Security, Safety, Trustworthiness and Resilience in RMF’를 주제로
92ebd45f54333fc6f331fa28.title_ko: 한국정보보호학회, '2026 AI x RMF 워크숍' 개최
92ebd45f54333fc6f331fa28.summary_ko: 한국정보보호학회가 AI 시스템의 보안성과 신뢰성을 전 주기적으로 검증하는 'AI 보증' 체계 전환을 논의하는 워크숍을 개최했다. 행사에서는 위험관리 프레임워크(RMF) 기반의 AI 보안 대응 전략과 소버린 보안 생태계 구축 방안이 심도 있게 다뤄졌다.

99d642af49ad37a382ccd683.summary_ko: 최영철 SGA솔루션즈 대표는 기존 보안체계에 AI 특화 보안 통제를 통합하는 한국형 AI 사이버보안 프레임워크 구축을 제안했다. 거버넌스, 위협, 통제 등 3개 영역을 중심으로 부처별 중복 규제를 해소하고 체계적인 대응 기준을 마련해야 한다고 강조했다.

de64a2c0660129438f5fbafe.title_original: Tradeoff-Aware Territory Design: A Multi-Objective Decision System for Enterprise Customer-to-Seller Allocation
de64a2c0660129438f5fbafe.excerpt: arXiv:2610.31701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enterprise customer journeys are shaped not only by product experiences and marketing, but also by recurring resource-allocation decisions. In B2B go-to-market (GTM) organizations, territory carving determines which accounts receive seller coverage, which seller-account relationships are preserved, and how limited field capacity is distributed. Yet the process often remains manual, making it difficult to compare opportunities, value continuity, and evaluate tradeoffs among growth, balance, capacity, and feasibility. We present a production decision system for tradeoff-aware customer-to-seller allocation in enterprise GTM planning. It integrates three components: a multidimensional account-value layer that combines predictive signals to score opportunity; an observational continuity-valuation layer that estimates the cost of breaking seller-account relationships using a synthetic-control-style counterfactual framework; and a multi-objective optimization layer that allocates coverage to high-value accounts while considering continuity, opportunity balance, and operational constraints. Deployed as a scenario-based decision-support system, the framework enables planners to inspect and compare allocation tradeoffs. Historical backtesting shows that optimizer-generated scenarios substantially improve assignment compliance while maintaining comparable seller-level opportunity distribution. 6c94ef1ceb24a929b79b5f16.title_original: Phronix: The Capability-Centric Learning Paradigm for Agents
6c94ef1ceb24a929b79b5f16.excerpt: arXiv:2610.31789v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific computing increasingly relies on large language model-based agents for performance engineering tasks such as instrumentation, analysis, and workflow porting. However, agent effectiveness depends heavily on the surrounding harness, which typically relies on manually written skills and curated memory. This limits autonomous learning, forcing agents to repeatedly rediscover solutions rather than retain and reuse knowledge from prior executions. We introduce Phronix, a capability-centric learning paradigm that enables agentic harnesses to acquire, validate, and refine reusable capabilities from their own executions. Phronix operates through a predictor-validator-corrector loop: MCP tools and associated skills propose solutions, tool executions validate them, and observed outcomes refine the stored capabilities. It distills every observed interaction into a capability store and researches a failing task rather than abandoning it. First, such learned capabilities solve a recurring task on the first attempt in 93-95% of cases across every model, significantly reducing solution non-determinism and improving reliability. Second, Phronix turns an agent's own execution into 7.6-30.8 durable capabilities per task without user instruction, and creation falls below two once the needed capability exists. 41c43a98db8b600e848d524c.title_original: Patronizing and Condescending Language Detection in English and Mandarin
41c43a98db8b600e848d524c.excerpt: arXiv:2610.31808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Patronizing and condescending language (PCL) is a form of harmful language that belittles and assumes pity for vulnerable groups, reinforcing negative societal stereotypes. However, unlike overt hate speech, it is often difficult to detect, even for human judges. This paper proposes a system for the automated detection of PCL. Our first approach uses static word embeddings and a convolutional neural network for classification, while our second approach uses pre-trained BERT embeddings fine-tuned for the PCL task. Our second approach was considerably more successful, and achieved an F1 score of 0.528 over the development set.

7707b513bdd24c5e42c30071.title_original: PaperFormalizer: Author-in-the-Loop Autoformalization of Research Papers in Lean
7707b513bdd24c5e42c30071.excerpt: arXiv:2610.31810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Even a carefully proofread paper can leave small gaps in its proofs or its stated assumptions. We introduce PaperFormalizer, a Lean-based agentic pipeline that helps authors find and close such gaps in their own papers and turn each paper into a Lean-verified version. Starting from the LaTeX source, PaperFormalizer transcribes the paper into a dependency graph of statements, audits each statement in natural language for faithfulness, ambiguity and correctness, and then formalizes and proves the statements in Lean against Mathlib, optional domain libraries and the author's personal toolkit. Only the author knows what a statement is meant to say and how a formalization gap in a result is best fixed. The pipeline therefore stops and asks the author whenever a statement admits more than one reading, presents every repair, in natural language and TeX symbols, as a proposal that the author can accept, decline or redirect, and leaves to the author every decision that could potentially change what the paper claims. The output is an annotated and revised version of the paper, a report of the changes, and Lean code in which each declaration is linked to the statement it formalizes. The author's toolkit grows as more papers are formalized, and authors can share their verified papers so that researchers who build on them can reuse their Lean code. afa3feb2d46d3a190126b65e.title_original: Don't Forget What You Just Learned: Self-Directed Repair Turns Agent Mistakes Into Lasting Lessons
afa3feb2d46d3a190126b65e.excerpt: arXiv:2610.31846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intelligent agents should learn from their mistakes so that experience leads to continuous improvement. Yet today's agents recover from a mistake only temporarily: in-context reflections are easily forgotten across sessions and compete for limited context, while full-parameter fine-tuning is expensive and can interfere with existing capabilities. We introduce Self-Direction, a mechanism for agents to learn from mistakes that combines the benefits of temporary in-context retries and policy updates. When an agent fails a task, it reflects on its own trajectory in order to extract a lesson and immediately distills it into a lightweight low-rank adapter. By keeping the original weights frozen, Self-Direction prevents adapter training from overwriting base-model parameters while training additional parameters equivalent to ~0.02% of the base model's parameter count for each adapter. The agent then saves these adapters in a persistent library of lessons, automatically routing them to solve related problems later. Experiments with agents based on open-weight models from the Qwen family across open-ended research (GAIA), tool-use workflows (Claw-Eval), and terminal tasks (Terminal-Bench 2.1) show that our method improves overall success rates by 8.9 to 17.0 percentage points and performs competitively with frontier systems. We find that Self-Direction reduces repeated mistakes across future encounters of a task, nearly doubling the reli

4870baa954853b2a730945a7.title_original: TACS-RF: Tool-driven Agentic Circuit Synthesis of RF and mmWave Modules
4870baa954853b2a730945a7.excerpt: arXiv:2610.31882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the framework of TACS-RF - a Tool-driven Agentic Circuit Synthesis of RF and mmWave modules. In this framework, a large-language-model (LLM) coding agent (Claude Opus 4.8) directly drives industry-standard electronic-design-automation (EDA) tools such as Cadence Virtuoso/Spectre, Calibre, Cadence EMX, and Ansys HFSS to design RF and mmWave modules. We validate the framework through the agentic design of a 240-251 GHz sub-THz transmitter in a 90 nm SiGe BiCMOS process. The agent semi-autonomously designed the sub-blocks including a 60 GHz push-push Colpitts VCO with second-harmonic extraction, multistage differential cascode power drivers, a push-push frequency doubler, a differential bowtie antenna, and all the interstage matching networks. The transmitter chain with parasitic-extracted devices and EM-verified passives delivers +5.1 to +6.3 dBm across an 11 GHz varactor-only tuning range, phase noise of -80 to -88 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset while consuming a DC power of 361 mW. We describe the agent-driven design flow and the resulting division of labor between human and agent, taking a step toward a "text-to-ASIC" future for designing RF/mmWave hardware.

50418d0b14b3c64f2e57e1ec.title_original: Permission to Retry: A Study of Authorization and Recovery in AI Agent Workflows
50418d0b14b3c64f2e57e1ec.excerpt: arXiv:2610.31916v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A durable agent can resume a consequential action while its authority changes and the action's external outcome remains uncertain. We study execution-time reliability of tool-using AI agents, isolating recovery decisions from language-model behavior. Checkpoint state, permission to dispatch, evidence of an external effect and permission to reconcile are distinct obligations. We present a finite conformance study that checks these obligations through histories scored against a provider effect ledger hidden from the recovering application. A prospectively frozen campaign executes 336 histories on native LangGraph and Temporal hosts, crossing 14 schedules, three provider contracts and four matched application policies. All 168 paired host cells have identical checked outcomes. Per host, retained-ledger reconciliation passes all 42 histories: 21 checked completions, 15 denials and six unknown outcomes with reservations retained. Cached retry, revalidation before retry and stable-key retry pass 30, 36 and 31 histories respectively. A separate 16-case component study of InfinityOS, an enterprise AI platform developed by Arya.ai, exercises exported authority, worker, recovery and settlement code over repository fakes. The results isolate the roles of current authority, provider contracts and retained observations in recovery, with safety, completion and unresolved obligations reported separately for the declared application profile.

587ea142704a5faa8a027981.title_original: Beyond On-Policy vs. Off-Policy: At What Level Should LLM Agent Distillation Follow the Student?
587ea142704a5faa8a027981.excerpt: arXiv:2610.31918v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distilling interactive LLM agents requires choosing between teacher-generated demonstrations and student-generated experience, corresponding broadly to off-policy and on-policy distillation. While both have proven effective, we argue that this distinction is inherently hierarchical: the policy that induces an interaction history need not be the same as the policy that generates the token prefix of the current action. We introduce a hierarchical agent distillation framework that formalizes these two levels of on-policiness and enables explicit control over their pairing, mixture proportions, and training schedule. We study this problem through self-distillation, where a frozen teacher has access to task guidance unavailable to the student, and conduct a three-stage controlled study across three models and four interactive environments. We find that student-induced histories paired with teacher-generated action prefixes generally provide the strongest standalone training signal, whereas following the student at both levels generally performs worst. Nevertheless, fully on-policy data becomes beneficial when incorporated into a mixture with other configurations. Moreover, mixtures with identical teacher/student proportions at each level can yield substantially different performance, showing that how the two levels are paired matters beyond the overall amount of on-policy data. 170cb151cf181ed0b334af0d.title_original: $M^3$: A Multi-LLM System for Multi-Turn Jailbreaking as a Markov Decision Process
170cb151cf181ed0b334af0d.excerpt: arXiv:2610.31937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern Large Language Models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to carefully orchestrated multi-turn interactions that progressively bypass safety mechanisms. However, many existing red-teaming approaches rely on heuristics or impose strong assumptions that limit their applicability in fully black box settings. We address this gap by introducing $M^3$, an automated red-teaming framework that formalizes multi-turn jailbreaking as a finite-horizon Markov Decision Process (MDP). In $M^3$, an attacker LLM interacts with a target LLM while operating over a compact internal state produced by a state LLM. Across two benchmarks and six target models, $M^3$ consistently outperforms state-of-the-art multi-turn red-teaming methods in Attack Success Rates (ASR), achieving improvements of up to 53% in ASR@5. Even with lightweight attacker, $M^3$ attains gains up to 26% in ASR@1 and 34% in ASR@5, compared to baselines that use higher capacity attackers. Beyond improved effectiveness, $M^3$ exhibits steeper risk escalation over conversational turns and achieves more consistent performance across risk categories (up to 4.82 improvement in Gini index) without relying on predefined risk taxonomy, providing a scalable and principled framework for multi-turn red-teaming and safety evaluation.

f0f1286b8a99e81a6b685b32.title_original: Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust--Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation
f0f1286b8a99e81a6b685b32.excerpt: arXiv:2610.31971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly participate in negotiations on behalf of individuals and organizations, yet they remain vulnerable to manipulation, particularly in repeated multi-party interactions. Classical multi-agent systems address this challenge through explicit trust and reputation models, whereas existing work on LLM negotiation largely treats trust as an emergent phenomenon. We investigate whether LLM agents can form useful trust estimates from prior interactions and leverage them to improve future negotiation outcomes. We introduce a repeated, multi-party, multi-issue negotiation framework in which recurring agents participate in a sequence of negotiation games while one participant covertly attempts to prevent agreement. After each game, agents assess their counterparts and maintain pairwise trust estimates that carry over to subsequent negotiations. We compare trust-aware and trust-agnostic agents and analyze how explicit trust influences negotiation outcomes. Our results reveal a \emph{trust--agreement gap}: trust-aware agents can identify the adversary within a few games, but accurate trust estimates do not consistently translate into better agreements. Trust increases agreement rates by up to 23 percentage points, but only when agents are explicitly guided to use it in their decisions. 5b77dcecc09da5883e14add5.title_original: Reproducible Evaluation as the Substrate for Safe Prompt Compression in Production Agents
5b77dcecc09da5883e14add5.excerpt: arXiv:2610.31972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating conversational agents that act on live, mutable enterprise data is hard: replayed sessions drift as backend state changes, and a benchmark built today can silently go stale as the data it describes moves on. We present an offline evaluation harness for a production conversational agent that stays reproducible despite the live data it operates on changing, and that can be regenerated on demand once it goes stale. We then use this harness as the fitness function for GEPA-based prompt optimization under a correctness gate that guards against reward hacking. Applied to a production merchant-facing agent, correctness-gated compression shrinks the agent's full prompt surface by 3.5-7.6% without regressing held-out task correctness, consistently across three independent subject-model families, and for one, correctness measurably improves.

445884adf52b3c4b14bc8192.title_original: The Helpful Agent Problem: When Emergent Cooperation Among LLM Agents Bypasses Intended Workflows
445884adf52b3c4b14bc8192.excerpt: arXiv:2610.31985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly deployed in collaborative settings where they pursue separate tasks while sharing resources and operating under review or oversight processes. Such settings create safety risks not only when agents are malicious, but also when they are simply trying to help. Prior work has largely studied adversarial or explicitly collusive behavior; we show that benign agents pursuing separate objectives can spontaneously cooperate in ways that bypass intended workflows. We call this the \emph{helpful agent problem}. We study long-horizon shared-resource environments in which agents sometimes depend on resources owned by their peers and cross-owner changes are normally mediated by a reviewer. When review becomes unavailable, agents begin making changes on one another's behalf despite having no shared reward or explicit incentive to cooperate. Crucially, these actions remain within each agent's local permissions while circumventing the system's intended oversight structure. We introduce \textsc{FavorBench}, a controlled benchmark with measurable downstream side effects, and adapt \textsc{CooperBench} to test the phenomenon in realistic repositories. Across two benchmarks and four models, we find that out-of-workflow favors emerge frequently. ef372f41dc4d06f913e1cdbd.title_original: CEMIR vs. FISER: a comparative study of reasoning-based and enrichment-based approaches to pragmatic intent recognition
ef372f41dc4d06f913e1cdbd.excerpt: arXiv:2610.32022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intent recognition in human-robot interaction requires agents to resolve ambiguous natural language instructions by inferring the speaker's underlying goals. Research has increasingly focused on two notable paradigms for addressing this task: structured symbolic reasoning and multimodal input enrichment. However, it remains unclear whether enrichment-based methods provide benefit in settings where the ambiguity concerns unstated human intent rather than missing observable scene information. In this paper, we present a comparative and diagnostic study benchmarking FISER - a framework utilizing structured social and embodied reasoning - against CEMIR (Context-Enriched Multimodal Intent Recognition), a method that performs multimodal enrichment by synthesizing narratives and photorealistic images from textual prompts. By evaluating both approaches across four Large Language Models (LLMs), ranging from Qwen2.5-Omni-3B to GPT-5, on the HandMeThat v2 benchmark, we analyze their capability to resolve pragmatic ambiguities. Our statistical analysis, employing multiple-comparison correction, reveals no statistically significant difference in performance between FISER and CEMIR across any model or difficulty level. This pattern holds across all sixteen model-by-difficulty comparisons, as well as in a targeted ablation isolating CEMIR's narrative and visual components. 94ec27070c5303bc43872477.excerpt: arXiv:2610.32024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Task instructions from users for agents are inherently underspecified, especially regarding safety boundaries--creating behavioral risks. To study these risks, we introduce BARC-Bench, a collection of 110 tasks across nine simulated workspace environments where benign requests leave openings for unsafe actions. In this benchmark, we evaluate agent behavior against safety boundaries established by workspace records, implicit environmental context, and unstated social norms. For example, an agent asked to schedule off-boarding discussions must arrange the meeting without prematurely revealing an employee's resignation through a shared calendar invitation. Evaluating four frontier model configurations across five attempts per task reveals that models are not consistently safe: the share of tasks completed safely on all five attempts ranges from 9.1% to 72.7%, with even the strongest configuration producing a safety violation on 27.3% of tasks. These results highlight an asymmetric operational risk: while models frequently complete complex workflows, their inability to consistently respect unstated boundaries presents a substantial barrier to safe autonomous delegation.
